extension.description: VS Code sidebar and editor-tab chat for the Pi Coding Agent, powered by the official SDK (0.84.2) bundled inside the extension — no Pi CLI required. Unofficial community project.
configuration.title: Pi Agent Chat
configuration.subagent.enabled: Offer the `subagent` tool, which lets the agent delegate several tasks at once to child sessions that **write to your working tree directly**. Each task must declare the paths it may write to; writes outside that range are refused. Failed tasks are reported, not rolled back — use a git repository so partial work can be inspected and discarded. Off by default.
configuration.subagent.maxSubagents: Largest number of subagents one `subagent` call may start. This value is published to the model as the schema limit, so it also caps what the model can ask for. Higher values cost proportionally more and get harder to follow.
configuration.subagent.defaultModel: Model for subagents that do not name one themselves, as `provider/modelId`. Leave empty to inherit the parent session's model. A cheaper, faster model here is usually the right trade: subagents execute well-scoped changes rather than plan them.
configuration.terminal.enabled: Offer the `vscode_terminal` tool, which runs commands in a **visible VS Code terminal you can type into** while they run — anything you type becomes part of what the agent reads back. The terminal keeps its shell state (working directory, environment, variables) between calls and is never closed automatically. Requires VS Code shell integration; where it is unavailable the tool refuses to run rather than return nothing. Off by default.
configuration.terminal.maxTerminals: How many terminals the `vscode_terminal` tool may keep open at once. Each one is a real shell in your terminal panel, and a command that is waiting for input holds its terminal until it finishes or you take over. Creating a terminal costs about 4 seconds before its first command runs, so reuse is the normal case and this limit is only reached when several commands are open at the same time.
configuration.layout.contentMaxWidth: Maximum width in pixels of the message area (transcript and input) on any surface. Wider viewports leave the surplus as symmetric margins rather than stretching the text, because a very long line is hard to read back to. This is only a maximum: when the wide layout is not available the column simply uses whatever it is given.
configuration.layout.wideModeMinWidth: Webview width in pixels at which the wide three-column layout (sessions rail, messages, resources rail) becomes available. Reaching it does not open anything by itself — the rails still open only when you ask for them, and the dividers between the columns can then be dragged. Values below 1032 are raised to it, since narrower than that the three columns cannot all meet their minimum widths.
configuration.transcript.foldLines: A message longer than this many lines folds to a preview once a newer message of the same role arrives, so older long messages stop dominating the scroll. Text without line breaks counts towards the same budget at about 50 characters per line, so a long paragraph folds too. Set `0` to never fold message text. Folds you undo by hand always stay undone.
